offence_severity: Life imprisonment for Section 302 IPC / Rigorous imprisonment for three years for Section 506(11) IPC
physical_harm: Deceased sustained six serious bleeding injuries on the scalp, and DW2 sustained multiple injuries including fractures and lacerations
number_of_offences: Three offences/counts charged, all finally upheld by the trial court but set aside by the High Court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the prosecution story is not trustworthy and the evidence adduced on record is full of contradictions.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable, noting that the prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and that the evidence is full of contradictions.
trial_duration: The trial court passed the conviction order on 17th September, 1994. The High Court set aside the conviction on 22nd March, 2005. The Supreme Court judgment was delivered on 6th July, 2017.
legal_representation: Jayant Muth Raj, Ms. Malavika J., C. K. Sasi, Advs. for the Appellant; M. Karpaga Vinayagam, Sr. Adv., R. Nedumaran, S. Syed Mahaboob, M. Yogesh Kanna, Ms. Nithya, Ms. Maha Lakshmi, Partha Sarathi, Advs. for the Respondent.
investigation_status: Investigation in Crime No. 399/94 was continued for about three months and finally the proceedings were dropped by PW 11 - Inspector of Police for the reason that the accused in that case has already died on 15-09-1994.
procedural_irregularity: The High Court noted that the investigating agency ignored its paramount duty of bringing home the guilt of the accused with probable evidence as admissible under law, rather, spent time and mind on creating 'two occurrences and substantiating the same with the circumstances'.
appeal_history: The trial court convicted the accused. The High Court acquitted the accused. The Supreme Court upheld the acquittal of the accused.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were guilty beyond reasonable doubt, citing the testimony of the eye witness, the recovery of weapons used, the chemical analyst's report, and the statements of the doctors. They also emphasized the place of occurrence, the injuries on DW2, and the forensic reports with regard to blood stains on material objects and weapons used by the accused.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was fabricated, with the police creating two separate incidents and tampering with the FIR to create a wrong impression. They also contended that the deceased had raised violence upon DW2 and that the police had prevented the accused from taking the plea of self-defence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied judicial scrutiny to the facts and circumstances of the case, emphasizing that the prosecution must prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
precedent_relied_upon: Sadhu Saran Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. (2016) 4 SCC 357; Hare Krishna Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar (1988) 2 SCC 95; Appabhai & Anr. v. State of Gujarat (1988) Suppl. SCC 241; State of Andhra Pradesh v. Punati Ramulu & Ors. AIR 1993 SC 2644; Ashish Batham v. State of MP. (2002) 7 SCC 317; Joginder Singh v. State of Haryana (2014) 11 SCC 335
